segments.text: Imagine this your manager says please move the chairs one person moves five
chairs another moves every chair in the room another moves nothing because they
thought the task was for tomorrow who made the mistake maybe nobody maybe the
problem was not effort maybe the problem was communication great teams do not
only work hard great teams communicate clearly communication saves time it
prevents mistakes it builds trust and it helps people work well together the
biggest communication mistake is simple we assume we assume we understood we
assume the other person understood we assume everyone has the same picture in
their mind but different people can hear the same words and imagine completely
different results most communication problems begin with an assumption the
solution is simple clarify ask questions you can say I just want to check
that I understood can you show me what you mean what does a successful result
look like when do you need this finished is this the highest priority these
questions are not signs of weakness they are signs of professionalism they show
that you care about getting the work right imagine your manager says please
clean the kitchen one person washes the dishes another cleans the floor another
wipes the work tops another empties the rubbish everyone is working hard but
everyone has a different understanding of the task a short conversation at the
beginning could prevent confusion later you could ask which areas need to be
cleaned who is responsible for each task when does everything need to be finished
a two-minute conversation can save 30 minutes of correction good communication
is faster than fixing avoidable mistakes now think about listening many people
listen so they can answer great communicators listen so they can
understand when someone is speaking stop what you are doing when possible look
at the person listen carefully do not interrupt and when they finish repeat
back what you understood for example so if I understand correctly you would like
me to finish this before lunch or you would like these five chairs moved to
the meeting room before 10 o'clock is that correct this is called checking
your understanding it takes only a few seconds but those few seconds can
prevent hours of wasted work good communicators also notice what has not
been said sometimes the deadline is unclear sometimes the priority has
changed sometimes important information is missing so before you begin ask what
do I need to confirm what might be unclear what does the finished result need
to look like another important habit is checking in if a task takes several hours
or several days do not disappear give an update you can say just checking in is
this still the priority or this is my progress am I on the right track small
check-ins prevent big problems a task can begin correctly and still move in the
wrong direction priorities can change new information can arrive a short update
gives everyone the chance to adjust before time is wasted remember this bad
news does not improve with time if something will be late speak up early if
you made a mistake speak up early if you do not understand speak up early if you
need support speak up early people can help solve a problem they know about
they cannot solve a problem they do not know exists speaking up early is not
creating a problem it is giving the team time to solve it that is responsibility
that is trust and that is good communication communication is also
about respect when you communicate clearly you respect other people's time
when you listen carefully you respect the person speaking when you ask
questions you respect the work when you check your understanding you respect
the result and when you give updates you respect the whole team clear
communication also means choosing the right method some messages should be
sent immediately some are better discussed face-to-face some should be
written down a good communicator asks who needs to know when do they need to
know what is the clearest way to explain this because communication is not only
about what you say it is about what the other person understands so remember
four simple habits first do not assume second ask clarifying questions third
repeat back what you understood fourth check in early and often these habits
will make you a better teammate they will make you easier to trust they will
prevent avoidable mistakes and they will help the whole team succeed great
communication is not about using big words it is not about speaking more it is
about creating understanding the message is not complete when it is spoken the
message is complete when it is understood so communicate clearly listen
carefully ask questions give updates and clarify often because great teams do
not guess great teams make sure great teams understand one another and great
teams communicate
